text: Wednesday, seven a.m.: Nib eats cereal on the rooftop without his mask while Jaeha brushes his teeth.
Then someone pounds on the stair door.
Nib slaps on his mask and freezes like a doll, spoon still in his mouth.
It's Choi, with kimbap, coffee and a few questions. Of course, sir. Please come in.
Is his husk holding a spoon in its mouth? He likes holding things, sir.
Choi lays out kimbap and his incident report.
His Gate 0912 report has a hole. The boss was dead. Who killed it? Someone very brave, sir.
Nobody carried out a core worth hundreds of millions. Then somebody must have left it behind.
Choi reaches for the kimbap. Empty foil, and the husk's cheek is bulging.
His husk ate his kimbap. A very hungry husk, sir.
Then, off the record: men in very nice suits are asking about the survivors. And Black Hound is calling Jaeha a liar.
The polite mask slips. Nice suits don't ask about trap-testers unless they want something.
Leaving, Choi warns him: Mok hates looking stupid on camera. Jaeha is always careful. It's his only skill.
Choi tosses back one last kimbap, and the husk catches it blind. Very unusual husk.
Jaeha knows Mok's men. His notebook says they rig a job, then come back to check it. And they smoke menthols.
Today: an F-grade survey, ten thousand won a trap. And he's expecting one extra.
Hapjeong, two p.m.: F-grade Gate 2231, at the end of a closed shopping arcade.
The bored survey officer hands him chalk. Ten thousand per trap. Try not to die. It's a lot of paperwork.
Yerin insists on coming as team medic. It's an F-grade survey, he says. The most dangerous thing in there is dust.
By the gate: a fresh cigarette butt with a thin green band, and a boot print pointing in.
Jaeha's eyes narrow. A menthol.
Inside: a ruined granary of giant stone silos.
At a dark doorway, Nib holds out a palm. You first. He's supposed to be a husk. Husks don't have opinions. Nib does.
Jaeha uses Link to see through Nib's eyes as he scouts ahead. A plate on the fourth step.
A chalk X, and Nib steps around it.
Nib hangs upside down from a beam to point out a pit. Yerin counts: nine traps, ninety thousand won!
Then a round chamber, two chutes in the ceiling, a lever on a high ledge. Jaeha stops Yerin with one arm.
Through Nib's eyes: an old plate under a mound of clean grain, and a modern zip tie holding a chute's catch open.
That grain is clean, he whispers, when everything else has centuries of dust. And Far Side traps don't use zip ties.
Yerin goes pale. Somebody rigged this. Black Hound? Jaeha's answer: they smoke menthols.
Mok's men always come back to check. So he'll give them something to check.
He takes off his vest. Why? Because he's leaving them a body.
Nib shoves a stone block off the ledge onto the plate.
The chute bangs open, and tons of grain thunder down.
When the dust settles, his vest lies on the mound, an empty glove poking out like a hand.
On the ledge, Yerin calls it the creepiest thing he's ever done. They'll be back within the hour, he says.
Nib's notched ear twitches.
Two Black Hound men stroll in: the bald shield-bearer from Mok's back room, and a wiry trapper smoking a menthol.
The trap rat found his last trap, the trapper grins. The boss said make sure, and bring back his phone.
A menthol butt lands beside the empty glove.
The shield-bearer drives his sword down through the vest to make sure. If Jaeha had walked in first, that would have been him.
Yerin clamps her hands over her mouth. Jaeha doesn't move, eyes cold.
Then they kneel to dig for the body and the phone, right under the second chute.
The notebook snaps shut.
Jaeha and Nib haul the lever down together.
And a torrent of grain buries them both.
Buried to the armpits. He can't move anything!
Jaeha holds up his phone, recording. Good afternoon, gentlemen. Who sets a trap for a trap-tester?
The trapper frees one arm and aims a hand crossbow at Jaeha's eye.
Jaeha calmly points up. If he fires, the third silo comes down. It's right above his head.
A cracked hatch trembles overhead, trickling grain onto his face.
He drops the crossbow.
Who sent them, and why did he want the phone? The shield-bearer gives up. The boss said Jaeha recorded him.
Jaeha makes a polite call, bowing to nobody. Two hunters stuck in a silo in Gate 2231. Bring shovels.
Walking out, Yerin asks if that was true, about the third silo. He has no idea.
At dusk, officers haul the grain-covered pair up to the street. Bomi is waiting at the top.
Twelve traps, a hundred and fifty thousand won. One trap had two hunters in it.
Why are two Black Hound guys covered in rice? It's grain, miss. Long story.
Speaking of stories: she holds up the frozen sewer frame. Husks don't move like that, do they? She hasn't posted it. Yet.
Jaeha's smile freezes. Behind him, the husk's eye slides toward the phone.
Then, serious: she wants the real story, not to hurt anyone. And she needs a hundred thousand subscribers before her parents lose their restaurant.
The polite mask comes off. Two rules: never show his face, only film what he allows. One promise: when it's safe, she gets the story first.
Deal! And the Trap Rats are her exclusive. At waist height, Nib notes that nobody asked him.
Bomi squishes his cheeks. He talks! He's so cute! Nib radiates murder.
Across the street, a man in a black suit, earpiece in, silver hexagon pin on his lapel, lowers a long-lens camera.
That night, Jaeha stuffs his slashed vest deep into the laundry basket while Seoa types in her headphones.
But grain is trickling out of the pocket.
Seoa holds it up, one finger through the slash. He promised he'd quit.
The polite smile fails. One more gate, he promises. Just one more.
Seoa doesn't blink. That's what Dad said, the night of the Opening.
A memory: their father at the front door with his lunch bag, and outside the window, the sky turning red.
